trial: Randomized trial of adjuvant 5-FU-platinum vs paclitaxel-platinum for high-risk penile cancer
title: Adjuvant paclitaxel-platinum versus 5-FU-platinum in high-risk penile cancer
journal: Journal of the National Cancer Institute
population: 49 men with resected node-positive penile squamous cell carcinoma and at least one high-risk feature
summary: At median follow-up of 69 months, median DFS was 12.4 versus 19.6 months (HR 1.16, 95% CI 0.55–2.45; P=.686) and median OS was 21.3 versus 36.7 months (HR 1.13, 95% CI 0.52–2.44; P=.754) for 5-FU-platinum versus paclitaxel-platinum. Grade ≥3 toxicity was 77.3% versus 40.9%, grade ≥3 hematologic toxicity 54.5% versus 4.5%, and hospitalization for toxicity 45.5% versus 9.1%.
criticalReview: This is the first randomized comparison of adjuvant chemotherapy regimens in high-risk node-positive penile cancer. The study was stopped early and was underpowered for definitive efficacy comparisons, so the nonsignificant DFS and OS differences should not be interpreted as proof of equivalence. The clinically important signal is tolerability: paclitaxel-platinum substantially reduced severe toxicity, hematologic toxicity and hospitalization while improving treatment completion. The trial therefore provides an important treatment-burden signal but does not establish superiority for survival outcomes.
